 (Exparte)
 JUDGMENT The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 05-09-2020.

2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 05-09-2020 at about 5.00 p.m., the petitioner was standing in front of The Grill and Thrill Hotel, Kengeri Upanagara main road, near Vysala Circle, Kengeri Upanagara, Bengaluru, at that time the rider of the Bajaj Avenger Two-wheeler bearing No.KA-53-EM- 4141 ridden the same at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner and caused the accident.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Shekhar hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient and also under gone surgery.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 17 years and was studying in PUC and Sportsman.

Due to the injuries sustained in the accident,
petitioner is still under treatment and suffered permanent disability.

The respondent No.1 being the rider, respondent No.2 being the insurer and respondent No.3 being the RC Owner of the offending vehicle are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest.
3. In spite of service of summons, respondent No.1 and 3 - rider and owner have not appeared before the court, hence placed as Exparte.

After service of summons, the respondent No.2 Insurance Company has appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by denying the issuance of policy to the Bajaj Avenger Two-wheeler bearing No.KA- 53-EM-4141.
This respondent has issued a Policy bearing No.0206003121P105987354 in favour of first respondent in respect of Motor cycle bearing No.KA-53-EM-4141 and it is valid from 22-09-2021 to 21-09-2022.
However the said policy which does not cover risk of date of accident dated 05-09-2020.

Further contended that, there is no Likhit.C.M vs Ashok on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132965858/
2 compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.

sentences.text: Further it has denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
Further it has denied the cause and manner of accident and also the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the alleged accident and also the involvement of the offending car in the said accident.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is exorbitant and fanciful.

Accordingly prays to dismiss the claim petition against it.
4.

On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievious injuries due to the actionable negligent riding of Block Bajaj Avenger two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-53-EM-4141 by its rider, in RTA took place on 05.09.2020 at about 5.00 p.m near Vysala Circle, infront of the grill and Thrill Hotel, Kengeri Upanagara main road, Kengeri, Bengaluru?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
3. What order or award?
5. In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 16.
Further examined the Dr.R. Shashikantha, Assistant surgeon at Shekar Hospital, Bangalore as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P.16 to 20 and closed their side evidence.

On the other hand, respondent No.2 examined its official as RW-1 and got marked three documents at Ex.R1 to R.3 and closed their side evidence.
6.
Heard the arguments and perused evidence that are available on record.
7. My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : In the affirmative  Issue No.3 :

As per final orders  for the following:-
 : R E A S O N S:

ISSUE NO.1 :
8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as PW.1.

In support of his case, he has produced true copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar along with spot sketch, IMV report, AIR report, wound certificate, IMV notice and reply U/Sec.133 of MV Act and charge sheet which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 9.

3 9.
On perusal of Ex.P1- FIR is registered on the basis of the first information given by one Manjunath C.M. who was the father of petitioner.
The first informant has alleged about the negligence of the rider of Bajaj Avenger Two-wheeler bearing No.KA-53-EM-4141.
In continuation the IO conducted spot mahazar along with spot sketch as per Ex.P.3 and Ex.P.4.

As per the spot mahazar and sketch marked at Ex.P3 & 4 the accident spot is in the left side portion of the road and the accident was caused by the rider of the offending motorcycle by changing the lane.

Thereby it is evident that the rider of Bajaj Avenger Two-wheeler bearing No.KA-53-EM-4141 came to the extreme left side and was negligent in his riding, as such he was unable to control his vehicle and dashed against the pedestrian petitioner.
In the residential premises where the shops and houses are situated, the pedestrians are permitted to cross the road and the vehicles are expected to be proceed in a slow and cautious manner.
Thus the contents of Ex.P3 & P4 establishes the negligence of the rider of Bajaj Avenger Two-wheeler bearing No.KA-53- EM-4141.
Further, the Ex.P.5 being the IMV report discloses that the offending Bajaj Avenger Two-wheeler bearing No.KA-53-EM-4141 got damages in its front registration number plate and left side crash guard.

10. The petitioner examined himself as PW.1 by deposing the negligence of the rider of the Bajaj Avenger Two-wheeler bearing No.KA-53-EM-4141 and produced documents in support of his case to prove the alleged negligence.
The PW.1 was cross-examined at length by denying the negligence of the Bajaj Avenger Two-wheeler bearing No.KA-53-EM-4141 but nothing has been elicited to disprove the case of the petitioner.
Thereby the contention of the respondent No.2 in respect of contributory negligence of the petitioner cannot be accepted.
11. The Ex.P.9 is the charge sheet came to be filed on the rider of the Bajaj Avenger Two-wheeler bearing No.KA-53-EM-4141.
The IO has opined that the negligence is on the part of rider of the Bajaj Avenger Two-wheeler bearing No.KA-53-EM-4141.
No grounds are made out by the respondents to show that contributory negligence from the petitioner.

It is very important to note that if the rider of Bajaj Avenger Two-wheeler bearing No.KA-53-EM-4141 was in a controllable speed and if he was not negligent he could have controlled his vehicle before dashing the petitioner.

This shows the gross negligence of the rider of Bajaj Avenger Two- wheeler bearing No.KA-53-EM-4141.
12.
As discussed supra, the petitioner successfully established the actionable negligence by the rider of the Bajaj Avenger Two-wheeler bearing No.KA-53-EM-4141.

Thus, by considering all these points this court is of the opinion that the said accident is caused by the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the Bajaj Avenger Two- wheeler bearing No.KA-53-EM-4141.

By relying on the said precedent and in the absence of rebuttal evidence and denial in respect of police documents, this court is of the opinion that the accident has happened due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Bajaj Avenger Two-wheeler bearing No.KA-53-EM-4141.
14.

In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

entities.text: 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 15. Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

16. In this context by considering the contents of Ex.P1 to 9 this court tilts in favour of the petitioner as the petitioner has to prove the alleged negligence on the basis of the evidence and proof of the same on preponderance of probabilities.
17. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 05-09-2020 which is caused by the rider of the Bajaj Avenger Two-wheeler bearing No.KA- 53-EM-4141 which belonging to respondent No.3.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
18.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by the driver of the Bajaj Avenger Two-wheeler bearing No.KA-53-EM-4141.

Hence,
the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
a) PAIN AND AGONY:-
Petitioner has alleged that at the time of accident he was aged about 17 years.
As per Aadhaar card marked at Ex.P15 the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 22-07-2003.
The accident took place on 05-09-2020.
Hence as on the date of accident, petitioner was aged about 17 years.

As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P10 the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient at Shekhar hospital from 09- Likhit.C.M vs Ashok on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132965858/
5 09-2020 to 16-09-2020 for a period of 8 days and sustained displaced fracture both bone left leg and underwent operation on 14.09.2020 under spinal anaesthesia closed reduction and internal fixation of fracture of shaft of tibia/fibula was done.

sentences.text: By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.60,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.
b) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P12 amounting to Rs.1,40,106/- and receipts at Ex.P.13, amounting to Rs.37,725/-.
These bills are supported by the medical prescriptions.
The medical bills are not seriously disputed by the respondent and no grounds are made out to disbelieving these bills.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitled for the reimbursement of the same by rounding of the same i.e., Rs.1,78,000/-.
c) Loss of income during laid up period:
The petitioner has stated that he was a PUC Student at the time of accident.
To prove the said fact the petitioner has not produced any document.
In the cross-examination he has admitted that now he is studying LLB.
In the absence of any document the notional income of the petitioner is considered at Rs.14,500/- p.m. as the accident is of the year 2020.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P10 petitioner was admitted to Shekhar Hospital and underwent the operation.

Thereafter usually the healing period has to be considered for which in the absence of evidence, this court is of the opinion that in total four months period may be considered under this head as a loss of income.
So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.14,500 X 4 months = Rs.58,000/- during the laid up period.

d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by him the petitioner examined Dr. R.
Shahsikanth, Orthopedic Surgeon as PW.2, through him Clinical notes with disability assessment report, MLC register extract and police intimation, inpatient case details and X-ray are marked at Ex.P16 to P20.

According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained displaced fracture of both bones tibia and fibula of the left leg and underwent operation on 14.09.2020 under spinal anaesthesia closed reduction and internal fixation of fracture of shaft of tibia/fibula was done.
PW.2 being treated doctor of the petitioner assessed disability.
Petitioner suffered disability of right and left leg at 38% and to the whole body at 12.6%.
According to the petitioner he was a PUC student also sports man and suffered with displaced fracture of both bones tibia and fibula of the left leg.
The disability caused to the petitioner may affect on his future career to greater extent.
Hence, I hold that the petitioner sustained disability of 10% to the whole body.
As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '18'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.14,500/- X 12 X 18 X 10% =Rs.3,13,200/- which is the total loss of future income.

6 e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE;
As per discharge summary, the petitioner was admitted to Victoria Hospital and took treatment as inpatient and underwent surgery.
As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P7 the injuries sustained by the petitioner are grievous in nature.
By considering the nature of injuries and the period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.
Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
f) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner admitted to Shekhar Hospital as per Ex.P10 and underwent surgery for the fractures sustained by him.
There is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

But by considering the nature of the injuries as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges of Rs.8,000/- - in total as he was inpatient for a period of 8 days in the hospital as pleaded in the petition.
g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.35,000/- under this head.

7 20. Liability:-

According to the petitioner, the respondent No.1 is the rider,
respondent No. 2 is the insurer and respondent No.3 is the owner of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-53-EM-4141.
The respondent No.2 in its objection statement has denied the issuance policy to the offending motorcycle bearing No. vehicle bearing No.KA-53-EM-4141.

The respondent No.2 insurance company has taken specific defence that the policy number mentioned by the petitioners is a fake policy and they have not issued any policy in respect of motorcycle bearing No.
KA-53-EM-4141.
21.
In support of their said defence, the official of respondent No.2 examined as RW.1 and Ex.R.1 to R.3 are marked.

On perusal of Ex.R.3 as argued by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 the policy number:
0718833119P109414443 is belongs to their company which was issued for vehicle bearing No.KA-01-P-5442 which is Maruthi Suzuki Omni Car for the period of 15- 10-2019 to 14-10-2020 and the policy number as mentioned in the plaint i.e., policy bearing No.071883311P109414443 does not belongs to their company and they have not issued any policy to motorcycle bearing No. KA-53-EM-4141.
The respondent No.3 being the owner of said motorcycle bearing No. KA- 53-EM-4141 has not disputed the allegation of non- issuance of policy by R2.
In this case, even after the service of summons, the respondent No.3 remained exparte.
When the respondent No.2 has denied the existence of policy, it is the burden on the petitioner and respondent No.3 owner to show that the vehicle was duly insured.
22. The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 relied on the following judgment ILR 1997 KAR 1061 between The Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., V/s. N.S. Devaraja and Others, "11.

sentences.text:
The Division Bench disapproved such an approach of the Tribunal in that case and it observed as under:
"In our opinion the approach made by the Tribunal is totally erroneous.
The Insurance Company cannot be expected to prove the negative.

When the Insurance Company stated in its objection statement that the vehicle was not insured with the Insurance Company, the burden of proving that the vehicle was insured with the appellant insurance company lay either on the petitioner- Claimant or on the owner of the vehicle.
If really the insurance policy was in existence nothing prevented the owner of the vehicle to" produce a copy of the insurance policy.
It was also open for the petitioner to secure information from the Motor Vehicles Department as to whether the vehicle had been insured and placed it before the Tribunal.

In the absence of any such evidence adduced either on behalf of the claimant- petitioner or on behalf of the owner of the vehicle, the Tribunal should have proceeded on the basis that the plea taken by the insurance company in the objections statement was correct."
ILR 1997 KAR 1980 between The Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., V/s. Chikkegowda and Others,

sentences.text: 5. Under the Motor Vehicles Act of 1939 as well as 1988 the registering authority or the Police Officer is required to furnish the particulars of the vehicle involved in the accident and as such it is not as if the insurance particulars cannot be secured at all.

When once the insurance company disputes its liability to indemnify the liability of the owner of the vehicle on the ground that the insurance particulars are not given, it is for the claimants or the owner of the vehicle to place material on record to indicate that the vehicle was insured on the relevant date.

This Court in NEW INDIA ASSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED v. NARAYAN BALAJI KULKARNI AND OTHERS MFA 282/83 has held that it is not for the insurance company to prove that the vehicle is not insured with them and that it is either for the claimants or the owner of the vehicle to prove that the vehicle was actually insured with the company when the fact of insurance was disputed.
6.

sentences.text: In the present case, the claimants have produced the notice issued by the police with regard to the accident.
In that notice the column meant for showing the name and particulars of the insurer and the number of the insurance policy has been left blank.
There is no other material on record to indicate that the vehicle in question was insured with the appellant.
In the circumstances, the insurer cannot be made liable for the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
23. Thereby there is a prima-facie onus on the petitioner to prove that the respondent No.2 has issued the policy to the offending vehicle.

In this regard no doubt that the petitioner mentioned the policy number as policy bearing No.071883311P109414443 and when the petitioner was cross-examined he has stated that he has furnished the said policy number on the basis of Ex.P.6 and he has not seen any policy cop and also in the charge sheet the police have invoked the sections against the owner of the offending vehicle for not having insurance for the offending vehicle at the time of accident.

The answers given by the PW1 is hereby quoted:

sentences.text: 24. On perusal of Ex.P.9 certified copy of the charge sheet it is found that the investigation officer also found that the offending motorcycle was not insured at the time of accident, as such Sec.146 and 196 of IMV Act was invoked against the respondent No.3 herein who is the owner of the offending motorcycle.
The Ex.P.6 is an AIR report where the policy details as policy bearing No.071883311P109414443 valid from 15-10-2019 to 14- 10-2020 is mentioned.
But in the Ex.P8 reply given by the owner to the notice issued under Sec.133 IMV Act, they have not furnished any policy details.
In the charge sheet itself the investigation officer found that there was no insurance to the offending vehicle at the time of accident.
Merely because some policy number is mentioned in AIR report it cannot be said that the respondent No.2 insurance company is liable to pay compensation on behalf of respondent No.3 owner.

The petitioner as answered in his cross-examination as per the information obtained by the petitioner through crime records, he has furnished the policy particulars, but the respondent No.2 denies the issuance of policy to the said car.
25. It is the duty of the respondent No.3 to appear and furnish the proper policy particulars.
Just because the respondent No.3 owner remained exparte, the liability cannot be fixed on the respondent No.2 insurance company on the basis of some policy number is available in the AIR report.
The investigation officer himself found that there was no policy for the offending vehicle at the time of accident.
The petitioner not choosen to examine the investigation officer to explain the contradiction between Ex.P.8 IMV reply, Ex.P.6 AIR report and Ex.P.9 charge sheet.
In the absence of policy and contract, the respondent No.3 being the owner liable to pay the compensation along with interest to the petitioner @ 6% p.a.
Accordingly, issue No.3 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
26.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s. 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petition against respondent No.2 is hereby dismissed.

 JUDGMENT The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 05-09-2020.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident,
petitioner is still under treatment and suffered permanent disability.
The respondent No.1 being the rider, respondent No.2 being the insurer and respondent No.3 being the RC Owner of the offending vehicle are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
opennyai_summary.issue:
On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.
Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievious injuries due to the actionable negligent riding of Block Bajaj Avenger two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-53-EM-4141 by its rider, in RTA took place on 05.09.2020 at about 5.00 p.m near Vysala Circle, infront of the grill and Thrill Hotel, Kengeri Upanagara main road, Kengeri, Bengaluru?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
3. What order or award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Proceedings under Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a Civil Court.
Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this Likhit.C.M vs Ashok on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132965858/
4 regard.
13.
By relying on the said precedent and in the absence of rebuttal evidence and denial in respect of police documents, this court is of the opinion that the accident has happened due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Bajaj Avenger Two-wheeler bearing No.KA-53-EM-4141.
14.
In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.
17. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.
When the respondent No.2 has denied the existence of policy, it is the burden on the petitioner and respondent No.3 owner to show that the vehicle was duly insured.
When I so observe, with reference to the doctrine of burden of proof, I find support from the Division Bench Decision of this Court in NEW INDIA ASSURANCE COMPANY LTD., v.
NARAYAN BALAJI KULKARNI AND ORS *MFA No. 282/1983 dt. 11.1.1990 decided on 11th January 1990 by Division Bench consisting of Hon'ble Mr. Justice M. Rama Jois and Hon'ble Mr.
Justice S.R. Rajasekhara Murthy.
ILR 1997 KAR 1980 between The Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., V/s. Chikkegowda and Others,
5. Under the Motor Vehicles Act of 1939 as well as 1988 the registering authority or the Police Officer is required to furnish the particulars of the vehicle involved in the accident and as such it is not as if the insurance particulars cannot be secured at all.
When once the insurance company disputes its liability to indemnify the liability of the owner of the vehicle on the ground that the insurance particulars are not given, it is for the claimants or the owner of the vehicle to place material on record to indicate that the vehicle was insured on the relevant date.
This Court in NEW INDIA ASSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED v. NARAYAN BALAJI KULKARNI AND OTHERS MFA 282/83 has held that it is not for the insurance company to prove that the vehicle is not insured with them and that it is either for the claimants or the owner of the vehicle to prove that the vehicle was actually insured with the company when the fact of insurance was disputed.
6.
In the present case, the claimants have produced the notice issued by the police with regard to the accident.
In that notice the column meant for showing the name and particulars of the insurer and the number of the insurance policy has been left blank.
There is no other material on record to indicate that the vehicle in question was insured with the appellant.
In the circumstances, the insurer cannot be made liable for the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
23. Thereby there is a prima-facie onus on the petitioner to prove that the respondent No.2 has issued the policy to the offending vehicle.
In the charge sheet itself the investigation officer found that there was no insurance to the offending vehicle at the time of accident.
Merely because some policy number is mentioned in AIR report it cannot be said that the respondent No.2 insurance company is liable to pay compensation on behalf of respondent No.3 owner.
25. It is the duty of the respondent No.3 to appear and furnish the proper policy particulars.
Just because the respondent No.3 owner remained exparte, the liability cannot be fixed on the respondent No.2 insurance company on the basis of some policy number is available in the AIR report.
The investigation officer himself found that there was no policy for the offending vehicle at the time of accident.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s. 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petition against respondent No.2 is hereby dismissed.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.6,82,200/- (Rupees Six lakhs eighty two thousand two hundred only) along with interest at the rate of 6% from the date of petition till realization of the amount.
The respondent No.3-owner is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of the compensation amount awarded, it is ordered to release entire amount in favour of petitioner on proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
